en: When using Codex, whenever you start a new
session by restarting Codex in the CLI or by
starting a new thread in the desktop app or
the IDE integration,
you get a new essentially empty context
window. Essentially empty because a system
prompt will be included and some basic
instructions, but other than that, there's
nothing in there. It especially doesn't know
anything about prior conversations or
sessions you might have had with Now,
if you want to resume an older session, if
you wanna get that context and that
discussion and output from back then back so
that you can continue it, you can get there
in the CLI by running
/resume and then picking the session you
wanna pick up on and continue.
Or with the IDE integration, you can choose
from the list of tasks up here and you can
also expand that list. A similar feature, of
course, exists in the native app. There you
have all your threads there on the left, and
you can simply switch between them. And
therefore, this can be a useful feature if
you wanna continue a conversation or working
on a task, and that old context matters to
you.
